findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified with a group handle as reviewer; nothing in the text shows an SME actually ran the multi-arm SPL against real ingress, kube-state-metrics and OTel data.
findings.suggested_fix: Lower status to draft until a named Kubernetes/ingress SME has validated it on live data and recorded the date.

findings.explanation: The SPL only has an NGINX arm and a Traefik arm, so only two of these controller_family values can ever be produced; dataSources, equipment (envoy, haproxy, azure) and the scope paragraph also claim Envoy, HAProxy, ALB, GKE and Application Gateway coverage that the search does not implement.
findings.quote: Document controller_family values in your runbook: nginx_ingress, traefik, envoy_ingress, haproxy_ingress, contour_envoy, aws_alb, gke_l7, aks_appgw.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add arms for the other controllers or restrict description, dataSources, equipment and scope to NGINX Ingress and Traefik and describe the others as separate follow-on work.

findings.explanation: Scheduling a 15-minute alert over a 24-hour window re-evaluates every historical 15-minute bucket on each run, so one incident keeps matching for a day (throttling hides but does not remove this) and the three 24-hour joins to metrics are expensive. Step 3 also says to alert on critical or high, while the SPL `where` keeps medium, and the final `true(), "medium"` branch turns every remaining row into an alert.
findings.quote: save uc_3_2_18_ingress_upstream_backend_5xx every fifteen minutes with earliest=-24h@h latest=now
findings.suggested_fix: Use a short lookback (for example the last two to three 15-minute buckets) for alerting and keep 24h only for investigation; align the severity filter between prose and SPL.

findings.explanation: The four scenarios are title/field word salad (batch `sum`, synthetic probe on `_time`) and none names a real cause of a spurious 502/503/504 burst, such as rolling deployments, intentional scale-to-zero, load-test or scanner traffic, planned backend maintenance, or health-check endpoints returning 503.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `cluster` without crossing `rt_raw` > 0 for UC-3.2.18.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with real ingress false-positive causes, each with how to distinguish it, and key suppression on vhost/namespace.

findings.explanation: The CIM Performance data model describes host CPU, memory, storage and network metrics; it does not carry HTTP response_time per vhost, so mapping ingress access logs to it looks wrong. Web is the dataset that fits access logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the CIM Performance dataset fields; remove Performance from cimModels unless a real mapping exists.

findings.explanation: The grounding guide names Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes and Splunk Connect for Kubernetes; a 'Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes' is not listed, and the data sources give no Splunkbase ID for the access-log parsing (nginx:access, traefik:access sourcetypes appear to be local conventions).
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes documentation for legacy HEC patterns
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the add-on name or remove it; state that nginx:access and traefik:access are locally assigned sourcetypes and what props are needed.

findings.explanation: Authoring-process instruction leaked into reader-facing documentation; the section also duplicates the full SPL.
findings.quote: Fenced SPL for runbooks must match the spl JSON field byte-for-byte aside from newline normalization:
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the authoring note and keep only a brief pointer to the saved search.

findings.explanation: Describes only the NGINX arm and omits Traefik, the kube-state-metrics joins and the on-call routing, and the group-by list omits namespace and vhost that the SPL actually uses.
findings.suggested_fix: State that each row is a 15-minute bucket per cluster, namespace and vhost with 502-504 counts joined to endpoint availability and pod readiness.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Traefik JSON access-log `Duration` is reported in nanoseconds (see https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/observability/access-logs/), but the SPL treats `rt_raw` below 300 as seconds and anything else as milliseconds, so req_latency_ms and p90_latency_ms would be inflated enormously and always exceed LAT_WARN_MS. Verify units.

For NGINX the namespace is coalesced from `proxy_upstream_name`, which has the form `<namespace>-<service>-<port>`, not a namespace; the later joins to kube_endpoint and pod readiness on cluster+namespace will then not match, defaulting to 'healthy' via fillnull(999999 / 1) and masking zero-endpoint outages.

The metric joins parse `namespace="..."` and trailing values from `_raw`, assuming Prometheus text exposition; events delivered via the OTel splunk_hec exporter are typically JSON, so these rex extractions may never match.
The leading `comment("...")` macro and the embedded `UC-3.2.18` identifier: the comment macro is not a built-in; confirm it is defined, and avoid putting the UC ID inside SPL text.

Joins Web.url (aliased vhost) to Performance.dest on 15-minute buckets, and uses Performance.response_time, which is not a field of the CIM Performance model; the join key is not semantically comparable.

summary: A substantive and well-differentiated ingress 502/503/504 detection with a genuinely useful implementation walkthrough, undermined by template description/false-positive text, claims of coverage for controllers the SPL does not handle, a verified status without sign-off, and a 24-hour re-evaluation window that will re-alert. Several field and unit assumptions need verification.
